title: The Process Choice That Broke Even at 10,000 Units, Not 5,000
featured_title: THE PROCESS CHOICE THAT BROKE EVEN AT 10000 UNITS NOT 5000
subject: other-disciplines

presentation.challenge: The fixed-cost difference was correct, but break-even depends on the difference in variable costs. The correct crossover is 10,000 units.

practice.primary_question: How is break-even quantity calculated between two alternatives with different fixed and variable costs?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Dividing fixed-cost difference by one option's variable cost instead of the variable-cost difference.

case_dna.target_misconception: Break-even is ΔF divided by one alternative's variable cost.
case_dna.why_plausible: The fixed-cost difference is correctly identified, but both alternatives have variable costs.
case_dna.corrected_model: Set total costs equal or divide the fixed-cost difference by the variable-cost difference.

problem_statement: Process A has fixed cost $80,000/year and variable cost $12/unit. Process B has fixed cost $140,000/year and variable cost $6/unit. Determine break-even quantity and the lower-cost option at 15,000 units/year.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The fixed-cost difference was right. The denominator was wrong.
gates.prompt: What variable-cost term belongs in the denominator?

options.label: Set 80,000+12Q=140,000+6Q
options.reason: Break-even occurs when total costs are equal.

options.label: Use 60,000/(12+6)
options.reason: The incremental rate is the difference, not the sum.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Intersect the cost lines
gates.result: The alternatives break even at 10,000 units/year.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove break-even
gates.hint: Move fixed costs to one side and variable-cost terms to the other.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Lower variable cost offsets higher fixed cost

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the break-even note
report: C1. B has $60,000 more fixed cost.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is A's stated variable cost.

evidence_choices.label: 60,000/(12-6)=10,000 units
evidence_choices.reason: This uses the incremental variable cost.

options.label: Choose A because fixed cost is lower
options.reason: Above break-even, B's lower variable cost dominates.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply break-even again

options.label: About 2,667 units
options.reason: That divides by only one variable-cost rate.

gates.explanation: Use the fixed-cost difference divided by the variable-cost difference.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the analysis
gates.confirmation: I confirm that break-even is found by equating total costs.

items.label: What failed
items.value: ΔF was divided by one variable-cost rate.
